title: AI Is Changing Music. Its Future Must Be Built Around Artists (Guest Column)
summary: SoundCloud CEO Eliah Seton pens an open letter detailing the company's new AI policies.
contentText:
At SoundCloud, we believe the future of music should be artist-first. Our brand and our business have been built on the trust artists place in us, and protecting that is fundamental to who we are. Being artist-first is the lens through which we approach AI, recognizing both its potential to expand creative possibilities and the risks it presents to artists, their rights and the communities they build. Technology will keep changing how music is made. Our responsibility to protect the artists who make it won’t.

Too often, AI is framed as a binary choice: all good or all bad, embrace it or reject it. It is time that we address this transformation with the nuance that artists deserve. The reality is that AI presents existential risks if managed wrong and game-changing opportunities if managed right. It is our responsibility to artists to both minimize those risks and maximize those opportunities.

Innovation and Artist Protection Must Evolve Together

Every major shift in music has challenged our understanding of what it means to create. From sampling and synthesizers to auto-tune and digital production, new technologies have consistently pushed the boundaries of creativity, opened doors for new artists, and given rise to entirely new genres and sounds.

But music has never been created in isolation. Collaboration, shared experimentation, and the exchange of ideas between artists has always been central to how new sounds and genres emerge. As AI transforms the creative process, we must ensure it doesn’t displace the spaces where artists connect, collaborate, and inspire one another.

History shows us that innovation and artist protections don’t have to be opposing forces. They can and must evolve together, on behalf of artists.

Artists must have a voice in shaping what comes next. Through artist roundtables and ongoing dialogue with creators and partners across not only our own platform, but Reddit, Discord and beyond, we’re listening to how artists are using new technologies, where they see opportunity and what concerns them. Those perspectives inform the products we build, the policies we adopt, and the partnerships we pursue. Being artist-first means giving artists a meaningful role in defining SoundCloud’s future.

The Recorded Music Industry Wants Labels on AI Music. How Could That Work? (FAQ)

Protecting Authentic Creativity and Platform Integrity

Today, we are announcing updates to our Community Guidelines and Terms of Use to combat spam, fraud and deceptive activity on SoundCloud.

These updates focus on two areas designed to protect the integrity of SoundCloud and create a more trustworthy experience for artists and fans.

- Addressing Slop and Spam : AI slop has no place on SoundCloud. We are drawing a clear line against AI slop, spam, and excessive uploads that overwhelm the platform, interfere with music discovery, or undermine the experience for artists and fans. SoundCloud has always been a place for artists to freely share their work, experiment, and push creative boundaries. But creative freedom does not extend to abusive practices that compromise platform integrity or make it harder for authentic artists and their music to be discovered.

- Preventing AI-Enabled Fraud and Manipulation : SoundCloud will not tolerate the deceptive use of AI to manipulate platform systems, exploit creator opportunities, or mislead artists and fans. This includes misrepresenting the origin of content or the identity of a creator, such as falsely presenting AI-generated music as entirely human-made or portraying an AI-generated persona as a real human artist

AI should be a tool for creativity, not a means to deceive, exploit, or game the system.

Copyright Protection : Respect for copyright and intellectual property is fundamental to protecting artists and their work. At SoundCloud, we are committed to safeguarding the rights of all creators and rights holders, from independent artists to major labels who use our platform to share and discover music, build audiences and connect with fans. As the technological, regulatory and contractual landscape around AI evolves, so too will our approach to upholding these rights, but our commitment to protecting them will not.

Expanding Opportunities for Artists and Fans

Protecting artists is only part of our responsibility. We must also equip them with technologies that expand creative possibilities and unlock new opportunities. Simply wishing AI away won’t make it disappear. It will only leave the future of this technology to those who may not share our commitment to artists, putting their work at greater risk of exploitation or being crowded out. We have a responsibility to help shape what comes next, ensuring AI expands opportunities for artists rather than undermining them.

SoundCloud to Allow Direct Music Purchases

For creators , we’re focused on tools that expand creative possibilities and help artists build sustainable careers. Our recently announced partnerships with Moises and ElevenLabs expand access to innovative tools for music creation and collaboration. Both partnerships reflect our commitment to working with companies that use ethically trained AI, prioritize transparency, and respect creator rights. Today, SoundCloud works with more than 10 approved AI partners that share these commitments, with more to come. As AI changes how music is made, direct publishing integrations also give us greater visibility into AI-generated content entering SoundCloud and a better understanding of where that music originates.

For fans , AI isn’t new to SoundCloud. We’ve long used machine learning to improve music discovery, including through our acquisition of Musiio and personalized recommendations. Programs like Amplify build on our broader commitment to helping emerging artists reach listeners. We’re harnessing our AI and machine learning capabilities to make discovery more powerful, more personalized, and more uniquely SoundCloud. Fans come here to find what’s next: new artists, new sounds, and emerging scenes before they break into the mainstream. Our technology helps make those connections happen, bringing real artists and real music to the audiences who will move culture forward.

Looking ahead, we see opportunities to make discovery even more personalized while giving fans greater control over their experience.

Building Trust Through Transparency and User Choice

As AI becomes more prevalent in music creation, transparency and user choice are more important than ever. SoundCloud has always been a place where fans actively seek out new sounds, discover emerging artists and dig deeper into the music and communities they love. As the volume of music being created continues to grow, giving listeners greater agency over their discovery experience becomes even more important. That means strengthening platform protections, increasing transparency and preserving the sense of exploration and connection that has always defined SoundCloud.

Transparency is an important part of that commitment, but it’s not as simple as applying a label. Distinguishing fully AI-generated music from music created with AI-assisted tools is complex, and industry standards for labeling and detection are still evolving. Through our approved AI partner integrations, we display identification information provided by partners, giving listeners greater
visibility into where music comes from and how it was made.
